title: Code Generation and Maintenance at Scale: Morgante Pell
talk_summary: He also details edit-format economics (output tokens dominate cost) and why language-server-style incremental validation beats full rebuilds.

takeaways.technique: Compiler/linter feedback loop as the core agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: After generating code, they build/type-check it and feed the compiler errors back to the model to fix, rather than asking the model to self-diagnose. They note this flow is 'probably half of what you need' for a good agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this basic flow of prompt get some code uh build it type check it and then fix that output based on the LM this is actually really powerful
any time we actually have more than 10 prompts in a row uh our chance of having successful PR is dramatically lower
takeaways.numbers: >10 consecutive prompts sharply lowers PR success; 6-10 parallel agents from a known-good state; final chain only ~4 generations despite 30-40 total

takeaways.evidence_quote: we can actually take the in memory State snapshot that and then Fork it into 10 different isolated environments that all have everything pre-computed
takeaways.numbers: 10 min full build vs ~1s incremental recheck; 30s model generation dwarfed by 10min build

takeaways.technique: Loose search-and-replace edit format instead of whole-file or diff output
takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid regenerating whole files (laziness, expensive output tokens) and avoid unified diffs (bad line-number math, off-distribution) and JSON function calls (escaping overhead); they use a loose before/after snippet match.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you really don't want to Output entire large files as you're making edits you want to find a good edit format
takeaways.numbers: Output tokens ~3-5x input price (GPT-4o 5:15, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 3:15); output limits ~4k tokens even with 1.5-2M context

takeaways.technique: Static-analysis + semantic hybrid code search, not pure RAG
takeaways.what_they_do: They combine syntactic queries (function calls, import graph traversal) with embedding similarity to find exactly the edit sites, arguing pure chunk-and-embed RAG retrieves irrelevant context and has unpredictable result counts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you just go to try to find stuff that looks like looks like a logging error uh it's going to find a lot of irrelevant context

takeaways.technique: One orchestrator engineer/agent driving many sub-agents on a coordinated change
takeaways.what_they_do: A single principal-level driver plans the change and delegates per-file edits to sub-agents, replacing cross-team coordination meetings; the rest of the team just reviews incoming PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have one engineer who is actually coordinating that change is driving a individual AI developer agent to do the changes
takeaways.numbers: Migration postponed for years done in a week; <100 developer hours + thousands of compute hours
